books.section: Topic 2.5 Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.misconception: The revolt was not purely economic — the rebels destroyed churches and killed priests.
options.text: The rebels had been so thoroughly Christianized that their uprising was purely an economic protest.

options.misconception: The revolt was violent; hundreds of Spaniards were killed and Santa Fe was besieged.
options.text: The rebels limited themselves to peaceful, nonviolent forms of protest against Spanish rule.
The rebels attacked Spanish religious and cultural symbols as well as the colonial labor system.

options.misconception: The rebels were not protesting a tax; they rose to expel the Spanish entirely.

rationales.A: The revolt was not purely economic — the rebels destroyed churches and killed priests.
rationales.B: The revolt was violent. Background: hundreds of Spaniards were killed and Santa Fe was besieged.
rationales.C: Josephe describes a wholesale rejection: the rebels burned churches, destroyed Christian images, mocked sacred objects, and killed priests — and at the same time they threw off the forced-labor system that exploited them. The revolt attacked the two things Spain had imposed together, religion and labor, because the Pueblo people experienced them together, as a single system of rule. It was not a protest about one grievance; it was a refusal of the whole colonial order.
rationales.D: The rebels were not protesting a tax; they rose to expel the Spanish entirely.
rationales.general:
1. List what the rebels attacked. Churches, images, sacred objects, priests — and the labor system.
2. Ask why both at once. The Pueblo people experienced religion and labor together, as a single system of rule.
3. Name the revolt. Not a protest about one grievance, but a refusal of the whole colonial order.
Remember: when a revolt attacks two things together, the two things were one system to the people who lived under it.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
stem: Josephe's testimony indicates that the Pueblo rebels did which of the following?

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the 1681 interrogation of Josephe.
stimulus.text: Asked what drove the rebels to renounce Spanish authority, Josephe — a Spanish-speaking Pueblo Indian questioned by colonial officials after the 1680 uprising — answered that the causes were the ill treatment they suffered: Spanish officials beat them, seized their property, and forced them to work without pay. Asked why the rebels burned churches and images, mocked sacred objects, and killed priests, Josephe said he had heard it stated that while besieging the Spanish villa the rebels shouted that the Spaniards' God was dead and that only their own gods lived. Their captains ordered that the names of Jesus and Mary never be spoken, and Josephe reported seeing new houses of native worship built where the people danced their traditional ceremonial dances. — paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
